title: First record of a Trichodesmium sp. bloom in an extratropical region of the argentine continental shelf and its possible relationship with the outbreak of Alexandrium species
content:
Abstract
A bloom of the subtropical cyanobacteria Trichodesmium sp. has been reported in the north of the Argentine continental shelf (36° 54′ 12,0′′ S–55° 55′ 06,0′′ W), which coincided with positive and persistent sea surface temperature anomalies and preceded an unusual bioluminescent bloom of Alexandrium species further south. Based on these observations, the objectives were (i) to taxonomically identify the species responsible for both blooms using optical microscopy, pigment composition and toxin profiles; (ii) to characterize the spatiotemporal distribution of the Trichodesmium bloom by applying a specific satellite algorithm; and (iii) to correlate the oceanographic and meteorological conditions (temperature, salinity, currents and winds) with the recorded blooms. The Trichodesmium sp. bloom caused an orange surface color change that persisted for at least 10 days and spread in a SW–NE direction for more than 150 kilometers, close to the 50 m isobath. At least Alexandrium catenella and Alexandrium affine were identified in the Alexandrium bloom. Paralytic shellfish toxins were detected in the second bloom, but not in the first one. Given that Trichodesmium sp. produces ammonium and Alexandrium’s ability to incorporate it, we discuss the possible interrelationship between these blooms, and the implications of the potentially toxic effects in areas of fishing interest.
